newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal hits Bangladesh opposition leader's remark.
newsitem.headline: Nepal hits Bangladesh opposition leader's remark.

text.p: Nepal said on Tuesday it had protested remarks by Bangladeshi opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia that questioned the sovereignty of the Himalayan kingdom.

Khaleda, criticising recent moves by India and Bangladesh to forge a subregional trade bloc, earlier this month said the grouping would undermine the sovereignty of Bangladesh and that New Delhi "will treat us (Bangladesh) like Nepal and Bhutan".
"We feel hurt about the sentiments expressed by Khaleda Zia about Nepal," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said in Kathmandu.

Nepali diplomats said Nepal's ambassador in Dhaka, Lok Bahadur Shrestha, had communicated to Khaleda that the kingdom was "deeply hurt by the serious aspersions about the status of Nepal" made by the former prime minister.

Nepal and Bangladesh belong to the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), launched in 1985 to improve the living conditions of the region's more than one billion people. The other SAARC members are Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
In Dhaka, leaders of Khaleda's Bangladesh Nationalist Party could not be reached for comment or to confirm that she had received the protest letter from the Nepali Embassy.
